unresolvedQuestions: What actually draws the near-black amoeba patches on the hero plaza, and whether the critic's 'puddle' reading is right at all. Two independent bounds say they are not reachable from this file. Scale: the plaza is Props.groundMaterial, the cobble tile laid at GROUND_UV_SCALE 0.62, i.e. 1.61 m per tile, and its two weathering fields run at 27 cm and 31 cm — nothing authored in the tile can be a 2-3 m blob. Value: over the baked 256^2 tile the single darkest cobble albedo texel is 0.249 of the tile mean in linear luminance and the 1st percentile is 0.350; with Props' own weathering multiply (0.844 at its darkest) the absolute floor is 0.210. The critic's box (1304,977,89x53) reads luma p50 4.1 against the adjacent dry control's 43.6, which is 0.051 in linear — four times darker than the darkest albedo this file can produce, over an area three orders of magnitude larger than a texel. Light is being removed, not reflectance. The most likely candidate, and the one the r15 ablation was queued to test, is that these ARE the plaza's cast shadows and they are crushed to black; that would also reconcile the round's own blocker 2, which reports no cast shadows on the plaza while these patches sit on it. Owner: src/render/Lighting.js.

MaterialLibrary.addDetailNormal has zero call sites in src/. The shared detail-grain shader patch, which exists so close-range surfaces reveal grain the base tile has no resolution for, is never installed on any material. Terrain reads lib.detailNormal directly, so the texture is used but the layering patch is not.

Apparatus check that must be repeated by anyone scripting this rig: begin() in main.js is async and awaits audio.unlock() before menus.onGameStart(), so a menus.skipIntro() issued in the SAME page.evaluate() as __kagerouStart() is undone by the onGameStart() that follows it, and the title card's ink wash then sits over the world at full alpha. Start, wait for the engine to be ticking, cancel the intro, confirm _title < 0 and _titleA and _introWash are both <= 0.004, and only then call hud.__hide() — HUD.update clears the shared canvas exactly once when hidden and Menus keeps painting the card on top of it afterwards. R15-MAT-004 (met, three independent measurements): Materials.js is NOT the term eating the cool fill, and nothing is. (i) The code HANDOFF item 2 names, the TRI_AO block, is never compiled: MaterialLibrary.triplanarPatch has exactly one call site, Terrain.js:1608, and it is called with NO material, so the function returns at its first line and applyTriplanar never runs. (ii) The aoMap term that IS live is three's stock aomap_fragment with this file's per-recipe intensities; measured over each baked tile the effective indirect multiplier is cobble 0.962 (removes 3.8%), lanternStone 0.968, plaster 0.946, stone 0.900, cedar 0.897, dirt 0.786, roofTile 0.766 (removes 23.4%) — an order of magnitude short of the ~90% removal 'a tenth of the fill survives' requires. (iii) From the live rig read off window.__kagerou (sun intensity 3.4087, colour [1,0.4118,0.1339], elevation 12.99 deg; hemi 1.0197 on 0x6f8db8/0x4c3f31; scene.environmentIntensity 0.06431 delivering probe luminance 0.1815) the plaza illuminant is key [0.766,0.316,0.103] lum 0.396 plus fill [0.334,0.452,0.707] lum 0.446 — the fill is 52.9% of the illuminant, exactly as budgeted. Total illuminant B/R 0.735; times the measured cobble albedo linear B/R 0.700 gives reflected linear 0.515, approx sRGB 0.740, which brackets the two plaza boxes the critic measured (lit 0.635, 'shaded' 0.822). The frame is doing what its inputs say.

R15-MAT-006 (cross-owner ceiling, for sky): HANDOFF item 2's 'illuminant fitted from the frame's own pixels is B/R 0.141' is confounded — a fit from pixels alone returns illuminant x albedo, and these albedos are warm by authored construction: cobble linear B/R 0.700, stone 0.712, lanternStone 0.735, plaster 0.857, cedar 0.519, dirt 0.369, vermilion 0.032. On valley that confound is larger still, because Terrain multiplies dirt by (0.58,0.46,0.35), a further 0.60 on B/R. Consequence for critic target (a), B/R >= 1.30 on the shaded haiden facade: that facade is Level.js wallMaterial 'plaster'. At a vertical normal the hemisphere mixes 50/50 with groundColor 0x4c3f31, so the delivered fill B/R is 1.648, not ARCHITECTURE §5's 4.01. With the key removed entirely, fill x plaster albedo tops out at approx sRGB B/R 1.170, and x cedar at 0.932. Target (a) is therefore NOT reachable by changing the key/fill ratio: the fill's own vertical-normal B/R must rise from 1.648 to >= 2.084 for plaster (+26%) or >= 3.441 for cedar (+109%). The levers are the hemisphere ground colour and the probe's spectrum, both in Lighting.js/Sky.js.
